newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds frozen in London as FOMC vigil sets in.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds frozen in London as FOMC vigil sets in.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were barely changed in London on Tuesday as a pre-FOMC vigil set into the market, traders said.
With most players already having set up or flattened their positions before the key Federal Open Market Committee meeting, analysts said any movements would be simply minor position adjustments.

"The turnover has picked up from Asia, but most of it has been in the two- to five-year paper," said one trader at a U.S. bank in London. "Activity is likely to stay pretty light before tonight's decision."
Dealers were not expecting any news from the FOMC until around 1800 or 1900 GMT -- well after London trading hours are finished.
The key 30-year benchmark long bond was trading at 96-21 by 0844 GMT, unchanged from Tokyo's bid close but slightly firmer than the New York 96-19 bid close.
December T-bond futures were quoted 3/32 higher at 108-06 in automated trade by the same time, while the 10-year U.S. yield spread aginst Germany was 75 basis points.

A slim majority of analysts polled last week by Reuters said they expected the Fed to tighten policy after the meeting. Of those, all but one said they expected a 25 basis point hike, while the other said a move of 50 basis points was on the cards.
But analysts said the relief likely to wash over the market if no interest rate move were made was likely to be merely a knee-jerk reaction.
"If the Fed decides to leave rates unchanged we should see a rally with yield curve steepening," said one London-based analyst in a research note.
"However the rally could prove short-lived with the market quickly turning to the next meeting on November 13."
But before any decision on interest rates emerges, the market faces September consumer confidence and August import price data from the U.S.
Analysts polled by Reuters are forecasting a 107.0 reading on consumer confidence versus 109.4 in August.
Dealers said auctions of two and five-year paper due on Wednesday and Thursday would then capture the market's attention -- but said there were risks involved.

"Very few people are in a position to get prepared for the auctions what with the FOMC meeting today," said the U.S. bank's trader. "I think its going to be a quick scramble after the (rate) decision is out of the way."
